transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because when I start eating my comfort foods, I can’t seem to stop. I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but my hand just keeps going back to the pot.
After these episodes of overeating, do you do anything to try to make up for the food you ate, such as making yourself throw up?
I’m not really sure what you mean by making up for it. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself doing anything afterward, other than feeling bad about how much I ate.
Did this pattern of overeating begin after a specific stressful event or difficult situation in your life?
Yes. It started after my close friend died. It’s been about three months now.

latest_inference.note: Overeating directly triggered by bereavement (death of a close friend) specifically aligns with F50.4 (Overeating associated with other psychological disturbances / psychogenic overeating), ruling out F50.8.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of uncontrollable comfort eating suggests binge eating behavior, putting binge eating disorder, bulimia nervosa, overeating associated with psychological disturbance, and anorexia nervosa (binge-eating subtype) in the differential.
